scope: Your route: ordinary non-in-service MD/MS through MCC 50% All India Quota in state government colleges, across 18 preferred states/UTs. Central, deemed, DNB, AFMS and INI routes have separate contracts.
aiq_answer: MCC allotment does not waive an applicable service bond. Read the AIQ-specific years and evidence column first. In Andhra Pradesh, the checked one-year undertaking explicitly names State/CQ seats, so an AIQ duration remains unconfirmed. Delhi has no single duration: MAMC is one year from 2025–26 onwards; other campuses require their own rule.
delhi_answer: Do not assume Delhi is free of post-PG service bonds. MAMC circular dated 7 August 2025 expressly introduces one year / Rs20 lakh for PG entrants from 2025–26 onwards, AIQ and state quota. DU's 2026 Rs10 lakh surety is a separate course-exit bond. Other Delhi campuses need their own current authority/cohort check.
limitation: A mixed-date evidence comparison, not a fully verified 2026 national bond schedule or a legal enforceability opinion. Unresolved terms remain unknown, never zero. Sources checked 18 October 2026; apply subsequent amendments.
definitions: Service bond: work owed after successful completion. The quoted amount is a default liability, not an annual fee or a charge automatically payable by every graduate.
Exit bond: liability for non-joining, resignation or discontinuation at specified stages. This is separate from compulsory service and counselling security-deposit forfeiture.

A bank guarantee or surety secures an obligation. Do not add it again to the underlying bond amount. Do not automatically add service and exit penalties; their triggers and interaction need the executed contract.

AIQ/MCC admission does not itself exempt a candidate from the admitting institution's applicable state service bond. Central/INI, private/deemed, state government and DNB contracts must be checked separately.
This comparison concerns ordinary non-in-service MD/MS entrants unless a row says otherwise. Diploma, DNB/DrNB, direct six-year courses, sponsored and in-service obligations are not interchangeable.
An old form, missing upload or silent prospectus is not proof of no bond. A checked 2026 rule is an admission-cycle snapshot, not a guarantee of the rule when a future graduate finishes.
checks: Obtain the latest government order, admission-year prospectus, corrigenda and the exact unsigned college bond before choice locking.
Confirm campus, qualification, branch, quota, admission year and whether any prior MBBS bond remains. Ask for the applicable clause in writing.
Confirm service duration, who posts you, location, specialty use, remuneration and whether a posting is guaranteed. A service obligation is not a guaranteed permanent government job.
Confirm maternity/medical leave, safety, housing, transfer and extension rules. Do not assume the service will be in Hyderabad or near home.
Confirm the deadline for offering/accepting a posting, release if no posting is made, and the process for obtaining a written discharge/NOC.
Confirm whether NEET-SS/INI-SS admission permits deferment, the bank guarantee required, and whether fellowship/observership has different treatment.
Confirm the financial formula: principal, pro-rata reduction, stipend/salary refund, interest, study expenditure and recovery costs. Ask how overlapping obligations interact.
Check exit dates, non-joining rules, remaining-course tuition, counselling deposit forfeiture and debarment separately.
Ask which originals, guarantees and sureties are requested and when they are released. A document describing retention is not an independent assessment of its legal enforceability.
Retain the signed contract and written answers. Recheck amendments before joining; seek qualified advice on an actual disputed demand.

institution_exceptions.finding: Positive service obligation, 2025–26 onwards: one year / Rs20 lakh for PG. DU Rs10 lakh exit surety is a separate obligation with different triggers.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: UCMS, LHMC and other DU-affiliated Delhi colleges
institution_exceptions.finding: DU 2026 course-exit surety established. Exact separate GNCT/college service implementation and admission cohort still need their own current order; no blanket no-service label.

VMMC/GGSIPU uploaded Rs3 lakh form concerns course exit. A current post-PG service determination for either institution is not established here; a RML DNB accreditation attachment is not a bond policy.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: AIIMS campuses, JIPMER, PGIMER and other INIs
institution_exceptions.finding: Check the exact INI-CET Part B, admission-year joining contract and sponsorship status. State geography alone does not establish the INI obligation or exemption. No current blanket no-bond finding is made in this dataset.
2026 clause 20.6 expressly prohibits post-PG service bonds within its scope. Course-exit/remaining-fee liabilities are separate; special trust/central/deemed contracts need independent checks.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: Private, deemed, charitable and DNB hospitals
institution_exceptions.finding: Check the exact quota and signed institutional contract. Some state terms extend beyond government campuses; Karnataka has a broad statutory form and MP form names private colleges. DNB is not automatically governed by an MD/MS table.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: Andhra Pradesh government colleges: State/CQ versus AIQ
institution_exceptions.finding: The current NTRUHS Annexure A is explicitly State/CQ, one year / Rs40 lakh. It does not establish that obligation for an AIQ entrant. Ask the chosen college for its AIQ service order; no positive AIQ exemption is claimed either.

The AP prospectus expressly assigns SVIMS its own tuition, training, stipend, bonds and service norms. Do not substitute the general AP State/CQ rule or label it bond-free without the SVIMS current admission contract.

MCC college bonds support one-year service if required. Gandhi form is 2025–26; Osmania service form is 2023–24. Confirm 2026–27 execution. A Rs50 lakh course-exit bond is distinct from Rs20 lakh MD/MS service liability.

AIQ is expressly included in the one-year requirement. Qualifying regular government/PSU appointment can permit release if joining-time extension is refused, with documentary conditions. SS degree relief exists; fellowship/observership is excluded from that relief.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: Odisha private colleges / government pre- and para-clinical departments
institution_exceptions.finding: 2026 admission guideline J(5) excepts private colleges from that bond-submission clause. In government colleges, pre/para-clinical doctors are assigned to medical colleges rather than the peripheral rotation; this is a placement distinction, not abolition of the two-year bond.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: Dr SN Jodhpur / Rajasthan state and society colleges
institution_exceptions.finding: AIQ non-service undertaking specifies two years. Its separate 2026–27 five-year / Rs80 lakh form is for in-service candidates. SMS 2025 branch values range Rs25 lakh to Rs1.5 crore. Do not transfer an outdated flat Rs25 lakh to every branch or assume an unverified government-job waiver.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: BHU / AMU and other central institutions in Uttar Pradesh
institution_exceptions.finding: The UP state-college two-year bond is not evidence for a central university. BHU’s checked 2025 junior-resident agreement concerns the three-year training and course-exit damages; it is not an affirmative current no-service certificate. Obtain the central institution’s own contract.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: Uttarakhand government colleges: subsidised tuition option
institution_exceptions.finding: Older Central/state-quota undertaking links two years of hill service to a subsidised-fee option. Its separate Doon form has different financial terms. Obtain the chosen campus’s current full-fee and subsidised-fee terms; do not assign historical fees, penalties or a zero-year option to every campus.

2019 resolution describes a limited exception for AIQ entrants already employed by central/other-state government or an instrumentality. It is not an exemption for an ordinary applicant simply joining via AIQ.

institution_exceptions.institution_group: AFMS institutions / AFMC Pune: Priority-V civilian PG entrants
institution_exceptions.finding: Separate AFMS route in MCC bulletin: five years of Armed Forces service on Short Service Commission, subject to commissioning/medical and age conditions. The checked bond specifies Rs60.5 lakh plus applicable interest under its default triggers. Do not replace this with Maharashtra’s ordinary one-year bond.
